Rumors suggest Apple will announce new products on October 13. Based on the timing of past October events, here is when Apple might announce the event date.

Will Apple hold an October event?

While the history of Apple's September events is typically quite consistent, the history of October events is far more inconsistent, with much greater variation in both the event date and the timing of the advance announcement.

Since 2010, Apple has held only ten October events, the most recent being the Halloween-themed "Scary Fast" event on October 30, 2023.

Below is the timing of Apple's advance announcements for each October event since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

That said, Bloomberg earlier reported that Apple plans to announce the long-rumored smart home hub, the next-generation HomePod mini, and an Apple TV 4K with next-generation Siri AI capabilities on October 13 (Tuesday), but did not indicate whether Apple would hold an event to announce these products.

If true, Apple could announce the event date as early as Monday, October 5, or as late as Wednesday, October 7.

It is worth noting that the market also expects Apple to announce an iPad mini with an OLED display, a new iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models in 2026, including one with a touchscreen. Whether these products will appear at the same event, be announced at another event, or be released via press release remains unknown.

Looking back, Apple announced new Macs via press release over three consecutive days in October 2024; in October 2025, the company announced the M5 chip and new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro models without holding an event.

By contrast, Apple has held only one event in November — the 2020 "One More Thing" event, at which it unveiled the first Macs powered by the M1 Apple chip.

Of course, 2020 was an unusual year for Apple's announcement schedule. After the rare delay of WWDC to late June, the pandemic disrupted the normal timeline, and the company held events in both September and October.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at the rumored October event? Let us know in the comments.
